title: Lease Fundamentals
description: Understand lease terminology, right-of-use assets, lease liabilities and the basic lessee accounting model.
html:
What is a lease?

A lease generally gives a customer the right to control the use of an identified asset for a period of time in exchange for consideration.

Important terminology

Lessee: The party obtaining the right to use the asset.

Lessor: The party providing the right to use the asset.

Right-of-Use Asset: Represents the lessee's right to use the underlying asset during the lease term.

Lease Liability: Represents the lessee's obligation to make lease payments.

Important idea

The lessee does not necessarily own the underlying asset.

Instead, the lessee recognizes its right to use the asset and its obligation to make lease payments.

Example

A company enters into a five-year lease for office space.

The company does not necessarily own the building. However, the lease may create both:

  • A right-of-use asset
  • A lease liability

Why leases matter

Lease contracts can create significant assets and liabilities, even though the company did not purchase the underlying asset.

Foundation

Think of lessee accounting as:

Right to Use Asset + Obligation to Pay
